policy.calibrationSelection: First 12 chronologically nonoverlapping mature forecast windows; selected missing labels fail the block without replacement
policy.testSelection: Later chronologically nonoverlapping mature forecast windows; origin strictly later than the final calibration target date

futureProtocol.requiredLabels: Same-bound issued prospective records with preserved completed target observations actually collected before the new information cutoff
futureProtocol.calibrationRule: First 12 chronologically nonoverlapping qualifying records; retain each original record ID, observation ID and exact residual; freeze the rank and radius
futureProtocol.issueRule: Issue a separately versioned calibrated forecast only after that block is fixed; preserve the unmodified raw forecast and its original record, and explicitly reference its model.sourceHash separately from the new calibration wrapper hash
futureProtocol.evaluationRule: Only later issued origins strictly after the final calibration target; preserve all selected missing and failed outcomes without substitution
futureProtocol.retuningRule: A changed seed, source graph, radius selection or calibration policy starts a different experiment and cannot inherit held-out scores

limitations: The first twelve nonoverlapping calibration windows and all later disjoint test windows are fixed before any test loss is calculated. Missing selected labels or controls are retained as incomplete, never replaced.
Forecast parameter fits may use all completed prices available at each forecast origin. The calibration radius alone is frozen and receives no later test residuals.
This is a new audit on already examined current-vintage development data. Chronological separation is not an untouched historical holdout, historical publication proof or prospective validation.
The rank ceil((n+1)*(1-alpha)) is an empirical order statistic. Serial dependence and regime shifts prevent asserting distribution-free ETH coverage from this calculation.
Coverage is reported as exact hit counts with one-case resolution. No IID binomial confidence interval, independent sample size, significance test or calibrated production probability is claimed.
Each candidate/horizon has its own available calibration block; compare only paired interval scores inside that exact test set, not cross-model table ranks.
The future contract requires new immutable calibrated records and actual previously collected prospective outcomes. Existing raw records and reconstructed historical residuals cannot be relabeled.
